title: Recurring Revenue Design
equation: Monthly Recurring Revenue = Customers × Price × Retention
hook: Starting every month at zero revenue is exhausting. Recurring revenue is how you stop doing that.
statement: Sell once, get paid again and again. Turn problems that keep coming back into recurring revenue.
explainer: One-time sales mean you're always hunting for the next customer. Recurring revenue stacks month over month, and good retention keeps what you already earned.
sop: List everything you sell as a one-time purchase.
Find which ones solve a problem that keeps coming back.
Package that into a subscription or membership with a clear rhythm.
Estimate Retention honestly: how many stay past month 3.
Work the weakest lever first: Customers, Price, or Retention.
equation_example: 200 Customers × $50 a month × 90% Retention = $9,000 MRR, your monthly recurring revenue. Raising price or retention grows it fastest without new customers. Lower retention quietly drains money you already earned.
question: Name one part of your business that could become recurring revenue within 90 days.
closing_statement: Sell it once, get paid on repeat.
caption:
Principle Nº 170: Recurring Revenue Design

Starting every month at zero revenue is exhausting. Recurring revenue is how you stop doing that.

Sell once, get paid again and again. Turn problems that keep coming back into recurring revenue.

Your turn: Name one part of your business that could become recurring revenue within 90 days.
